notice: Synthetic crew profiles (NEXUS-Med research, fictional NX-01 to NX-06). Measurement values follow published spaceflight trends; environment is real NASA RR-1 telemetry re-indexed to mission day, not measured with these crew profiles.

items.baselinePattern: HR 68; RR 14; T 36.6; SpO₂ 97%; sleep 7.0 h
items.dailyProgression: D10 sore throat/cough → D11 WATCH → D12 persistent multivariable change → D13-15 HR/RR/T↑ + SpO₂/sleep↓ → D14 red flag → recovery.
items.recommendedAction: Repeat measurements; reduce non-critical workload; open respiratory action card; CMO escalation during red-flag period.
items.whyUseful: Strong multimodal example using T°, HR, RR, SpO₂, sleep and symptoms.

items.dailyProgression: D16 thirst/reduced intake → urine and mass fall → HR↑/PA↓ → D20 flank discomfort/dark urine → persistent renal concern → hydration/recovery.
items.recommendedAction: Confirm hydration/urine pattern; reduce workload; follow renal/volume action card; CMO review if flank pain persists, fever or obstruction signs appear.
items.whyUseful: Uses history + urine + mass + HR + BP and demonstrates condition-specific context.

items.dailyProgression: Sleep gradually falls → fatigue/headache → HR and BP mildly increase → persistent change without neurological red flags → recovery intervention.
items.recommendedAction: Review sleep schedule/light/workload/CO₂; recovery period; repeat vitals; CMO if headache becomes severe or neuro/visual red flags appear.
items.whyUseful: Shows non-emergency persistent deterioration and explainable action without overdiagnosis.
